Comparative ecology and ecophysiology of some common pioneer plant species in Sarawak /
Institute of Biodiversity and Environmental Conservation.

Studies on the ecolong and ecophysiology of some common early successional species were carried out in the nursery of University Malaysia Sarawak, Sarawak, to investigate the effect of soil and nutrients on seddling growth performance. Soil properties were markedly affected by seedling establishment in several ways. Growth performances were significantly limited by soil nutrient availability. Analysis of variance show that the total biomass was significantly affected by the interaction between soil type and nutrient treatments in most of the study species.
Diversity and vertical distribution of moths (Lepidoptera:
Heterocera) in a tropical rainforest in Borneo /
Faculty of Resource Science and Technology.

The diversity and vertical distribution (ground, 1 m: subcanopy, 23 m: and canopy, 46 m) of the macromonths were investigated in a hill dipterocarp forest, Poring, Sabah, using modified Pennsylvanian light traps. A total of 1,169 species from 9,624 individuals and 15 families were recorded. The overall species diversity index for the macromoths was extremely high, that is 348.56+12.56 (95% confidence range). The overall total species richness and abundance demonstrated a bimodal pattern with the total richness and abundance culminating at the ground and canopy levels. The hill dipterocarp forest was characterized by the dominance of Noctuidae and Geometridae and the presence of the single species of the Borneon Brahmaeidae and seven rarely encountered species of Saturniidae.
Isolation and characterization of near complete cDNA and genomic sequences coding for granule-bound starch synthase in sago palm (Metroxylon sagu) /
Faculty of Resource Science and Technology

This study involved the isolation of a cDNA and a near complete genomic sequence that determine the granule-bound starch synthase (GBSS) gene from sago palm (Metroxylon, sagu). The cDNA was isolated via a reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) technique using primers designed based on the conserved regions of the GBSS. The RT-PCR product obtained, 917 bp in size, was cloned and sequenced. Homology search by using the BLASTX search program confirmed that the RT-PCR product consists of part of the GBSS gene, with the deduced amino acid sequence sharing 68-72% identities with GBSS of rice, potato, maize, wheat and cassava. A pair of specific internal primers was then designed based on the RT-PCR product. These primers were used to amplify the corresponding genomic DNA region via a genomic PCR method. A 2,008 bp genomic PCR product was generated by this primer set. Cloning and sequencing of the genomic PCR product confirmed that it consists of a partial genomic GBSS gene. This genomic PCR product was then used as a probe in an attempt to isolate the entire genomic locus of sago GBSS via Southern hybridization.
Isolation and characterisation of an endoglucanase gene from bacillus amyloliquefaciens strain UMAS1002 /
Faculty of Resource Science and Technology.

Gram-possitive bacterial species of the genus Bacillus are important sources of industrial enzymes such as amylases, cellulases and proteases. Much of the interest in these bacteria arises from their ability to secrete important enzymes at relatively high concentrations. Genes coding for such enzymes are valuable for application in industrial biotechnology. In this study, an endoglucanase A gene has been isolated from a Bacillus amyloliquefaciens strain (designated UMAS1002) that originated from sago waste compost. Molecular analyses were carried out to determine its organization and expression in different host strains. The ultimate aim was to enhance its ability to produce endoglucanase A for applications in industrial / environmental biotechnology.
Performance study of video transmission over internetworked ATM-Lan /

With existing video compression technology and standards, delivery of video and audio is made possible through distribution of media such as VCD and DVD. However this would require the end user to have a relatively powerful computer system and the corresponding hardware or software to ensure smooth playback. Using disc media as a form of content delivery also confines the service to only one user per one system at any time. Using the network enable many users to acquire the same video or to have wider variety of video for viewing from the local system without having to physically attain the media. This is made possible with the help of networking and video server. The main objective of the thesis work is to determine the internetwork performance between different network technologies through experimentation and the use of video streams. The different internetwork environments are identified and listed as network models in this thesis. These network models come about from observing the networks implemented on a real world environment, the campus network.
Acute pancreatitis a review of epidemiology prognostic factors and outcome /

Acute pacreatitis (AP) is one of the most important causes of acute abdoment. Advances in the pathophysiology and management of AP are being made at breathtaking pace. Thus a review of the local practice in the management of AP is lonv overdue. More specifically, this study covers several aspects of AP in the local population, namely the epidemiology of acute pancreatitis admissions to the University of Malaya Medical Centre (UMMC) between Jan 1995 and December 1999. At present, the severity of acute pancreatitis admisions in the UMMC is not routinely stratified using any preictive scoring systems as none of them has been validated in the Malaysian population. This study hope to determine the discriminatory value of the Imrie Scoring System in the local population as it is the only predictor used in the local practice. And finally, this study will look at a subgroup of patients with severe acute pancreatitis with regards to its complications, treatment and outcome.
